items.title: The Hanged Man and Temperance
items.short: patience and measure: waits calmly, does not break
paragraphs: Both energies are slow, and together they give a rare ability to live with uncertainty without strain. This person carries a long course of study or a long project through, and keeps going where the others quit.
There is little drive here on any front: no sharp decision, no demand for what is theirs. A whole life can pass in even waiting. One decisive action a year is the bare minimum for this pair.

seo.description: Both energies are slow, and together they give a rare ability to live with uncertainty without strain. This person carries a long course of study or a long project.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The Devil
items.short: sacrifice and craving: drawn to what hurts
paragraphs: A heavy combination: strong attraction plus a readiness to endure. From this come long dependent relationships, work that wears a person down, and explanations to oneself that this is how it must be and that it will soon get easier.

The way out always runs through stating the fact plainly: I feel bad here, and I am staying of my own will. From that point a choice appears; before it, the person counts themselves a victim of circumstances.

seo.description: A heavy combination: strong attraction plus a readiness to endure. From this come long dependent relationships, work that wears a person down.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The Tower
items.short: waiting and collapse: it held, then fell
paragraphs: The plot goes like this: a long suspended state with no way out, and then a sudden collapse that settles it. From the outside it looks tragic, but in fact it is the release the person never dared to arrange themselves.

Notice that the collapse arrives only after a long stretch of ignoring the obvious. Anyone who learns to speak up and leave in time gets the same changes without the disaster. The difference between these two versions is several years of a life.

seo.description: The plot goes like this: a long suspended state with no way out, and then a sudden collapse that settles it. From the outside it looks tragic.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The Star
items.short: waiting and hope: believes and waits
paragraphs: The Star gives faith, The Hanged Man gives patience, and a person can wait years for their own thing without losing the light. In long work — research, art, family — that is real strength.

Exactly that is the danger: hope lets you wait forever. Life settles into an “any moment now” mode that stretches on for decades. Deadlines help, the kind set for yourself and not announced to the world. It is useful to write down what changed over the year and read those notes out loud.

seo.description: The Star gives faith, The Hanged Man gives patience, and a person can wait years for their own thing without losing the light.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The Moon
items.short: a pause in fog: lives in a suspended feeling
paragraphs: Support here is blurred on both sides: the person lives in a state of uncertainty where nothing is settled and everything is felt. Good texts, good pictures and an understanding of other people’s pain come out of that place.

Everyday life and money fall through at the same time, and anxiety grows. Simple things keep such a person on the ground: sleep, meals at set hours, money in the account and one person with whom fears can be checked.

seo.description: Support here is blurred on both sides: the person lives in a state of uncertainty where nothing is settled and everything is felt.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The Sun
items.short: a pause in the light: waits, but not gloomily
paragraphs: A steady light keeps The Hanged Man from going dark: the person passes through the stops without despair, finds warmth in them and can enjoy small things. People like this take idle periods easily.

Recognition comes later than they would like, and they have to live with that. Those who stop comparing their pace with other people’s calmly live to see their own time; those who compare suffer for nothing.

seo.description: A steady light keeps The Hanged Man from going dark: the person passes through the stops without despair, finds warmth in them and can enjoy small things.

items.title: The Hanged Man and Judgement
items.short: sacrifice for a calling: pays for their own work
paragraphs: Meaning here arrives through refusal: the person leaves a good job for something unclear, loses income and status, and starts doing their own thing. A few years later it turns out to have been the only right move.

It is risky to turn that refusal into a feat and demand credit for it. A calling hands out no compensation, so it is better not to open an account: you chose it yourself, and that is all. Otherwise by fifty there is resentment towards people who promised nothing.

seo.description: Meaning here arrives through refusal: the person leaves a good job for something unclear, loses income and status, and starts doing their own thing.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The World
items.short: a long pause, a big result
paragraphs: A long road comes from The World and the stops along it from The Hanged Man, so life here moves more slowly than it does for everyone around. The result at the end of the road, though, is one that fast people never get.
Patience is there, but explaining it to the people close by is hard: from the outside it looks as if nothing is happening. Interim results shown to others help — at least once every two years.

seo.description: A long road comes from The World and the stops along it from The Hanged Man, so life here moves more slowly than it does for everyone around.

items.title: The Hanged Man and The Fool
items.short: pause and freedom: no action, no worry
paragraphs: A light and deceptive combination: the person can do nothing and not feel bad about it. Over a short stretch this saves them from fuss; over a long one it turns into a life that goes past them.

The difference between freedom and running away shows up in facts: what the person actually did last year. If there is no answer, the pause became a habit long ago rather than a rest. A pause with no answer to that question is just a way of deciding nothing.

seo.title: Arcana 12 and 22 together — The Hanged Man and The Fool
seo.description: A light and deceptive combination: the person can do nothing and not feel bad about it. Over a short stretch this saves them from fuss; over a long one it turns.

items.title: Death and Temperance
items.short: an ending with measure: closes gently
paragraphs: Temperance makes Death human: the person closes relationships and ventures without wreckage, with an explanation and with respect. People like this become the ones who help others through losses.

Gentleness sometimes drags the ending out: it feels a pity, it is frightening, it is awkward, and the dead thing lives on another year. The rule is simple — once a decision is made, the date is announced at once and not moved. Otherwise pity stretches the ending over years and spoils the good memories for both.

seo.title: Arcana 13 and 14 together — Death and Temperance
seo.description: Temperance makes Death human: the person closes relationships and ventures without wreckage, with an explanation and with respect.

items.title: Death and The Devil
items.short: passion and a cut: burns and burns out
paragraphs: A strong and dangerous pairing: attraction to the point of losing your head, and the ability to cut clean. Romances and ventures for such a person are bright, short and often end with a crash.

You can walk that circle for a long time, until a habit of waiting appears. Between “I want” and action — one day; between a row and a break-up — one week. The whole difference is built on that simple rule. Two rules like these are enough for life to stop coming apart in pieces.

items.title: Death and The Tower
items.short: a double break: everything changes to the ground
paragraphs: The harshest pair there is: both energies knock things down. Such a life splits into before and after several times, and each time what collapses is not a small thing but the base — home, work, family, faith.

Survival here comes through something simple: do not hold on, and do not explain to the world that it should not be like this. People with this pair usually have, by forty, an experience of rebuilding that others pay a lot of money to get.

seo.description: The harshest pair there is: both energies knock things down. Such a life splits into before and after several times, and each time what collapses is not a small.

items.title: Death and The Star
items.short: death and a star: hope after the end
paragraphs: After a loss such a person finds a new picture of the future faster than anyone else: they can believe when everything is in ruins. Hence the stories of “lost it all and two years later stood higher than before”.

Fooling yourself with a picture is easy too: instead of grieving, the person draws a new plan straight away. A loss that is lived through makes the next step steadier; a loss walked around comes back years later.

seo.title: Arcana 13 and 17 together — Death and The Star
seo.description: After a loss such a person finds a new picture of the future faster than anyone else: they can believe when everything is in ruins.

items.title: Death and The Moon
items.short: an end in fog: heavy partings
paragraphs: Partings for such a person are long and murky: first they feel it is over, then they live half a year in the unclear, then they cut. Neither energy has enough clarity, and that is the hardest part.

Saying out loud what is already understood helps, even when it is frightening. One honest conversation shortens six months of fog to a week and keeps people’s respect for each other. Drawn-out vagueness breaks more than the break-up itself.

seo.title: Arcana 13 and 18 together — Death and The Moon
seo.description: Partings for such a person are long and murky: first they feel it is over, then they live half a year in the unclear, then they cut.

items.title: Death and The Sun
items.short: the end and light: closes and moves on
paragraphs: Light keeps Death from pulling this person into the dark: they pass through losses and start shining again. They can say goodbye without hatred and then honestly enjoy something new, without looking back.

The speed of getting back up is sometimes too high: the grief is not lived through and there is already a smile in public. One conversation with someone you do not have to smile for closes that gap. Otherwise grief goes inwards and comes back years later with no reason at all.

seo.title: Arcana 13 and 19 together — Death and The Sun
seo.description: Light keeps Death from pulling this person into the dark: they pass through losses and start shining again. They can say goodbye without hatred and then honestly.

items.title: Death and Judgement
items.short: result and completion: sums up and closes
paragraphs: A double theme of the final: the person can finish and can judge what came of it. Often it is exactly this one in a family or in a business who sorts the archive, pays the debts and puts the full stop.

The hardest part is judging the losses: every ending goes through a trial of yourself. Splitting it out loud is useful — here is my part, and here are the circumstances that did not depend on me. That split brings strength back faster than any comfort.

seo.title: Arcana 13 and 20 together — Death and Judgement
seo.description: A double theme of the final: the person can finish and can judge what came of it. Often it is exactly this one in a family or in a business who sorts the archive.

items.title: Death and The World
items.short: a great completion: closes whole eras
paragraphs: Scale is set by The World, Death closes — and the person lives through big cycles whole: emigration, a change of profession at forty, a business handed over to others that lives on without them.

Between cycles there can be a long emptiness: the old is closed and the new has not appeared. Better not to fill such periods with the first thing that turns up; a pause with a clear end date works here. The emptiness passes by itself if the person is not frightened by it and does not fill it at random.

seo.description: Scale is set by The World, Death closes — and the person lives through big cycles whole: emigration, a change of profession at forty.

items.title: Death and The Fool
items.short: a free ending: leaves lightly and without goodbyes
paragraphs: Release comes from both sides here, so the person parts with the past remarkably easily: cities, jobs and people stay behind without drama. They can start from a blank page even at fifty.

Those left nearby get the most hurtful thing of all — a disappearance with no explanation. One short “I am leaving, and here is why” changes how they are remembered for years ahead and costs very little. People forgive a departure, but they do not forgive vanishing without a word.

seo.title: Arcana 13 and 22 together — Death and The Fool
seo.description: Release comes from both sides here, so the person parts with the past remarkably easily: cities, jobs and people stay behind without drama.

items.title: Temperance and The Devil
items.short: measure against passion: keeps a grip
paragraphs: Temperance damps down the extremes of The Devil, and the person gets strong desire with a working brake. They can want, they can earn, and they do not fall into dependence — a rare and very useful arrangement.

The brake weakens unnoticed: first a little is allowed, then it is every day. The sign that things are still fine is simple — being able to give up a familiar pleasure for a month and not look for a replacement.

seo.title: Arcana 14 and 15 together — Temperance and The Devil
seo.description: Temperance damps down the extremes of The Devil, and the person gets strong desire with a working brake. They can want, they can earn.

items.title: Temperance and The Tower
items.short: measure and a break: levels out after a collapse
paragraphs: The Tower knocks down, Temperance puts back together — the person goes through crises well and can assemble themselves again. Those who need to live through a catastrophe and keep their head are drawn to them.

Smoothness gets in the way of admitting in time that everything has fallen: the person tries to balance out what cannot be repaired. Sometimes the right answer is not to level it out but to close it and leave. One question tells the two apart: is this still alive, or already not.

seo.title: Arcana 14 and 16 together — Temperance and The Tower
seo.description: The Tower knocks down, Temperance puts back together — the person goes through crises well and can assemble themselves again.

items.title: Temperance and The Star
items.short: measure and inspiration: beautiful, without strain
paragraphs: The idea comes from The Star, and Temperance gives a steady walk towards it. Creative work for such a person reaches the end, because they do not burn out on the first excitement and do not drop it on the boring part.
Courage here runs short of what the pair really needs: big risky steps frighten both halves. One noticeable risk every few years is necessary here, otherwise everything stays neat and unnoticed.

seo.title: Arcana 14 and 17 together — Temperance and The Star
seo.description: The idea comes from The Star, and Temperance gives a steady walk towards it. Creative work for such a person reaches the end.

items.title: Temperance and The Moon
items.short: softness and sensitivity: supports by being there
paragraphs: Fine perception joined with measure gives a person next to whom others calm down. They feel the state another is in and do not press, so people who simply need to sit in silence come to them.

Boundaries of their own are almost absent here: someone else’s anxiety flows in freely and the person gets tired for no reason. An hour alone after every hard conversation is not a luxury but a condition of the work.

seo.description: Fine perception joined with measure gives a person next to whom others calm down. They feel the state another is in and do not press.

items.title: Temperance and The Sun
items.short: warmth and measure: calm joy
paragraphs: Next to such a person things are simple and good: they are even, warm, they make no storms and they can enjoy an ordinary day. People like this become the support of a family and favourite colleagues.
Life quietly becomes too smooth: no risk, no sharp wants, no voice of their own in an argument. Once a year it is useful to do something that scares you a little — otherwise calm turns into sleep.

items.title: Temperance and Judgement
items.short: measure and calling: walks to what is theirs at an even pace
paragraphs: Meaning arrives here without strain: the person finds their work and stays with it for years, building it up a little at a time. No sharp turns, no burnout — the long distance that actually produces a result.

Doubt comes from the slowness: it seems a calling ought to feel brighter than this. The honest test is simple — what have I done every single day for ten years with nobody pushing me? If there is an answer, the calling is already found; it just looks ordinary.

items.title: Temperance and The World
items.short: measure in a big undertaking: long and even
paragraphs: The World sets the length of the road, Temperance supplies a pace that can hold that length. People like this carry ten-year projects through to the end, and they rarely pay for it with burnout or with their relationships.

Visibility suffers: an even pace impresses nobody, and louder people move up instead. Public interim results help — once a year, short and to the point. The even pace then stops being invisible and starts building a name.

items.title: Temperance and The Fool
items.short: measure and freedom: light, but not empty
paragraphs: The Fool adds liveliness to Temperance, and the person stops being dull: calm without being tedious, flexible, quick to change shape, and still in balance in the middle of all the rushing about.

Commitments hold worse than they look: neither energy likes a rigid frame. What helps is a short list of firm agreements the person keeps in any circumstances. Everything else can shift with the mood and nothing breaks.

items.title: The Devil and The Tower
items.short: desire and collapse: wants hard and loses it
paragraphs: The pull of The Devil plus the break of The Tower makes for a life at high revs: the person gets hold of material things, loses them in a crisis and climbs back up again. By forty they usually know both big money and zero.

Attachments here are broken by the crash, not by a decision: it ends when everything has already fallen. Anyone who gets out earlier, by their own choice, saves ten years and half their strength. The trigger is rarely reason — usually it is the first real loss.

items.title: The Devil and The Star
items.short: wanting and dreaming: wants it beautiful and wants a lot
paragraphs: A picture is painted by The Star, and The Devil demands it right now and in solid form. Hence people with big taste and a big appetite: a beautiful home, expensive things, a business that looks like a photograph.
The gap between the picture and the money gets closed with credit, and that is the main trap. One rule covers it: earn first, buy afterwards — otherwise the dream turns into five years of payments.

items.title: The Devil and The Moon
items.short: dark pull: desire and fog
paragraphs: Of all the sensual combinations this is the heaviest: strong attraction plus blurred boundaries. The person ends up in stories that are hard to leave, and often cannot explain what keeps them there.

The work has to be done with facts rather than feelings: write down how many times you were promised a change, what it cost, what you actually got. A list like that sobers a person better than any persuasion.

items.title: The Devil and The Sun
items.short: desire in daylight: wants it and hides nothing
paragraphs: Open daylight drags The Devil out of the shadows: the person says plainly what they want, earns in the open and enjoys it without shame. This pairing works well in sales and in any public work.
The test arrives through success: money and attention together push the appetite up to an indecent size. What is being checked is the ability to give up something already familiar and pleasant.

seo.description: Open daylight drags The Devil out of the shadows: the person says plainly what they want, earns in the open and enjoys it without shame.

items.title: The Devil and Judgement
items.short: desire and a reckoning by conscience
paragraphs: Judgement asks The Devil about the price, and the person lives between a strong want and an inner prosecutor. At its best this makes a tough but honest dealer: takes what is theirs, and not over other people.

At its worst, guilt does not stop the deeds, it only spoils the pleasure. It is useful to decide in advance what is off limits for you — then there is nothing to justify to yourself once the deal is done.

items.title: The Devil and The World
items.short: a big pull: material work on a large scale
paragraphs: Appetite grows to the size of the horizon: one shop is not enough, a chain is needed; one deal is not enough, a market is needed. With that reach the person really does build something large, if the stamina lasts the distance.

Appetite easily outruns the means, and then everything falls at once. It helps to count what is built rather than what is wanted: how many parts already stand and bring in money without you. Measuring yourself by your plans is the most expensive habit here.

items.title: The Devil and The Fool
items.short: wanting and freedom: takes it and walks away
paragraphs: A hardy and risky pair: the person wants strongly and cannot bear obligations. They earn fast and drop everything just as fast, so their life story holds many beginnings and few finished things.

What saves them is anything written down: a contract, a share, savings. Without those, fifty arrives with rich experience and an empty account, and nothing left to explain it away with. Paperwork is the only thing that survives this kind of lightness.

items.title: The Tower and The Star
items.short: break and hope: sees something new after the fall
paragraphs: The Tower knocks things down, The Star immediately shows where to go next. Someone with this pair gets back on their feet after a disaster remarkably fast: while others are still grieving, they are already describing the next plan.
Grief walked around comes back later and heavier. Living a loss honestly is not weakness; it is how you avoid gathering up the leftovers ten years on in a counsellor’s office.

seo.description: The Tower knocks things down, The Star immediately shows where to go next.

items.title: The Tower and The Moon
items.short: collapse in fog: a fear that comes true
paragraphs: The sensitivity of The Moon plus the events of The Tower make a person who senses trouble coming and then gets it. Out of this grows either a heavy anxiousness or a rare skill for preparing in advance.

One thing decides which: what the person does with the premonition. Checked it, prepared, said it out loud — and it becomes a tool; carried it inside and was afraid of it — and it becomes a constant background.

seo.description: The sensitivity of The Moon plus the events of The Tower make a person who senses trouble coming and then gets it.

items.title: The Tower and The Sun
items.short: break and light: falls apart and shines again
paragraphs: Not even The Tower manages to put this person out for good: they go through losses and come back open and warm. Nobody speaks about crises more convincingly, because they came out the other side without turning bitter.
Playing the strong one too early is the trap here: a smile in public with nothing behind it. One person in front of whom you do not have to hold your face matters more here than any amount of advice.

seo.description: Not even The Tower manages to put this person out for good: they go through losses and come back open and warm.

items.title: The Tower and Judgement
items.short: break and calling: a crisis brings them to their own work
paragraphs: A collapse for this person almost always turns out to be the turn towards their life’s work: laid off — started their own thing; divorced — took up what they had been putting off. In hindsight it is very clear.

Resistance only makes the collapses repeat and grow stronger each time. Hearing it the first time is cheaper, although the first time always looks like plain bad luck. The second and third cost noticeably more than the first.

seo.description: A collapse for this person almost always turns out to be the turn towards their life’s work: laid off — started their own thing; divorced — took up what they had.

items.title: The Tower and The World
items.short: a big break: rebuilds an entire life
paragraphs: Wide scope from The World meets the demolition work of The Tower, and the changes turn out global: country, profession, circle, faith. The person starts over several times, and each time on a wider scale than before.

Roots barely have time to grow, and by fifty that is felt as tiredness. One unchanging thing helps: a place, a craft or people who stay through every move. That support is the difference between a traveller and a person with no roots.

items.title: The Tower and The Fool
items.short: a free collapse: wrecks it and laughs
paragraphs: The Fool makes The Tower bearable: the person loses things and does not fall apart, because they were never attached to what went. They change everything easily and treat a collapse as a change of scenery.

The people close by suffer more than they do: their lives come down too, and nobody asked them. One shared conversation before a sharp move keeps the relationship. A decision taken together costs less than months of resentment afterwards.

seo.description: The Fool makes The Tower bearable: the person loses things and does not fall apart, because they were never attached to what went.

items.title: The Star and The Moon
items.short: dream and fog: lives inside images
paragraphs: Fine perception from both sides: the person lives in a world of pictures, dreams and premonitions. In creative work and in mentoring that is an enormous advantage: they see what is not visible and can show it to others.

Ground is in catastrophic short supply: money, routine and paperwork all fall through. Boring things are what save the talent here — a budget for the week, an alarm set at the same hour, and one person who will tell the plain truth about reality.

items.title: The Star and The Sun
items.short: light and inspiration: sets people alight
paragraphs: The brightest pair of all: a vision plus warmth. The person talks about the future in a way that makes people follow, and does it without pressure. Project leaders and much-loved teachers come out of this mix.
Everything rests on response: without it the person dims and starts doubting their own picture. Keeping your own count of what you have done helps, so that the applause stops being the measure of it.

items.title: The Star and Judgement
items.short: image and calling: sees their own work in advance
paragraphs: The Star shows it, Judgement confirms it: the person understands early what they are meant to do, and usually recognises the work by a feeling of recognition. The whole of life is then built around that.

The gap between the vision and the current job can torment for years. An hour a day on your own subject helps — that hour is what moves a calling from a dream into a profession. After a year those hours add up to something you can see.

seo.description: The Star shows it, Judgement confirms it: the person understands early what they are meant to do, and usually recognises the work by a feeling of recognition.

items.title: The Star and The World
items.short: a big dream: a plan that takes a whole life
paragraphs: The World adds size to The Star: the plan comes out big enough to swallow a whole life — a book, a method, an institute, a business in several countries. Small ideas are not what this person invents.

Judging your own strength is where it fails: the start is run like a sprint while the road is twenty years long. Interim results are compulsory, otherwise emptiness sets in halfway. Breaking the plan into stages is not a formality here, it is how you live to see the end.

items.short: inspiration and freedom: lives on ideas
paragraphs: A light, lively pair: this person pours out ideas and cannot stand tight frames. They are interesting to be around, there is always a new plan in the air, and half of those plans are genuinely good.

Little of it gets finished: the interest lasts until the first boring part. One partner who likes to see things through turns this pair from fireworks into a result. Without such a person nearby, half of the good ideas stay as talk.

items.title: The Moon and The Sun
items.short: light and shadow: clear one week, dark the next
paragraphs: Two opposite states meet here, so life goes in waves: weeks of clarity and warmth, then a stretch of fog. Such a person can lift other people up and also understand those who feel low.

People around find these swings hard until they are explained. Saying it plainly to those close — I have dark weeks, they pass — removes half the conflicts. They stop guessing what they did wrong and simply wait for the bright week.

seo.description: Two opposite states meet here, so life goes in waves: weeks of clarity and warmth, then a stretch of fog. Such a person can lift other people up and also understand.

items.title: The Moon and Judgement
items.short: instinct and calling: hears the pull from inside
paragraphs: A vague sense of one’s own path arrives first, and Judgement later turns it into a decision. Usually a person carries the knowledge of what they should be doing for years, and then an outside event forces them to start.

The painful part is self-doubt: the signal is there, the proof is not. What helps is one small step taken without announcing it — that step gives the confirmation. Waiting for full certainty makes no sense here; it arrives only once the work is under way.

seo.description: A vague sense of one’s own path arrives first, and Judgement later turns it into a decision.

items.title: The Moon and The World
items.short: depth and breadth: senses the big currents
paragraphs: Perception widens out from people to everything around them: this person feels the mood of the times, of a scene, of a whole country. People like this are good at calling cultural and market turns.

Personal ground under the feet is weak here, and the sheer volume of impressions brings anxiety. The rule is simple: your own home and your own rest first, world currents second, otherwise they only frighten you.

seo.description: Perception widens out from people to everything around them: this person feels the mood of the times, of a scene, of a whole country.

items.title: The Moon and The Fool
items.short: fog and freedom: lives by feel
paragraphs: The Fool gives lightness, the Moon gives sensitivity, and this person lives by mood: plans change with the state of the day, they vanish and reappear without explaining. Inside there is a great deal that is fine and real.
Agreements hold badly here, and that hurts the people closest more than anything else. One firm promise, kept every single time, buys back all the rest of the freedom.

seo.description: The Fool gives lightness, the Moon gives sensitivity, and this person lives by mood: plans change with the state of the day.

items.title: The Sun and Judgement
items.short: light and reckoning: recognised for one’s own work
paragraphs: The Sun makes the calling visible: this person does their own work in the open and is recognised for it. By fifty such people usually have a name and a circle that knows it.

Other people’s opinion weighs too much here: without recognition the work starts to feel pointless. A useful question is whether I would still do this if nobody ever found out. The answer usually shows what is truly mine and what is done for an audience.

seo.description: The Sun makes the calling visible: this person does their own work in the open and is recognised for it. By fifty such people usually have a name and a circle.

items.title: The Sun and The World
items.short: a bright, large undertaking: shines wide
paragraphs: The scale comes from The World, the Sun adds openness, and this person becomes visible far beyond their own circle. Public life, teaching, work spread across several countries — that is the natural setting.

It burns a lot of strength, and the family ends up last in the queue. A simple check: if the public gets several times more hours than the people at home, the scale was bought at their expense. They need a fair share of attention, not the leftovers.

seo.description: The scale comes from The World, the Sun adds openness, and this person becomes visible far beyond their own circle.

items.title: The Sun and The Fool
items.short: warmth and ease: joy without obligations
paragraphs: The merriest pair of them all: warmth plus freedom. This person is easy to be with, lifts the mood of a room, makes friends fast and lets go just as easily. Loud company and children love them.

Serious things come hard: commitments, boredom, long labour. One piece of work carried to the end despite the boredom changes how this person sees themselves entirely. After that, lightness stops being a way of running away.

items.title: Judgement and The World
items.short: a reckoning on a large scale: builds big and finishes
paragraphs: Judgement adds things up, The World sets the size — this person takes on work that will outlive them and brings it to the point where it runs without them. Often that is a school, a method or a family business.

Such a project lives longer than any person’s patience, and doubt arrives right in the middle of it. Clear milestones help, and so do people who can be handed a part of it without the whole falling apart.

seo.description: Judgement adds things up, The World sets the size — this person takes on work that will outlive them and brings it to the point where it runs without them.

items.title: Judgement and The Fool
items.short: calling and freedom: own work, own rules
paragraphs: Judgement calls, the Fool refuses to march in step — so this person does their own work while breaking every accepted form. These are the people who found something new instead of fitting into the old.

The system finds this irritating, and recognition comes later than it does to the agreeable. Only their own interest keeps this person going; it is the single reliable support here. Waiting for the system’s approval is pointless — it is the last to arrive.

seo.description: Judgement calls, the Fool refuses to march in step — so this person does their own work while breaking every accepted form.

items.title: The World and The Fool
items.short: scale and freedom: the world as home
paragraphs: Neither energy tolerates cramped space: countries, languages and occupations change, and boredom never catches up. By fifty there is a life story others would not gather in two lifetimes.

Almost nothing settled is left: no house, no savings, no steady circle. A minimum of ground chosen on purpose makes this freedom bearable in old age. A little that stays put takes nothing from the freedom, but it makes later years calm.

seo.description: Neither energy tolerates cramped space: countries, languages and occupations change, and boredom never catches up.
